subject: chemistry
title: Weathering and Erosion
welcome_lead: Wind, water and ice slowly chew rocks into tiny grains. Welcome to weathering.
meta_desc: Learn weathering, erosion and transport in this KS3 chemistry adventure on rocks.
final_note: You can now explain how mountains turn into beaches.

concepts.def: Breaking rock into smaller pieces in place.
Freeze-thaw, plant roots, etc. break rock physically.
Acid rain or water dissolves parts of rock.
Plants and animals break rock down.
Sediment dropping out and settling somewhere new.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Physical: water gets into cracks, freezes, expands and splits the rock.
Chemical: acid rain reacts with minerals in the rock.
Biological: tree roots push cracks apart; lichens release acids.

Once a rock is broken into pieces, erosion carries them away. Wind, rivers, waves and glaciers all move sediment.

Weathering breaks. Erosion moves.
Eventually moving water or wind slows down and drops the sediment. This is deposition. Over millions of years, deposited layers can become sedimentary rock — and the cycle continues.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between weathering and erosion?
options: Weathering breaks rocks, erosion moves the pieces
